prompt.brief: Design Instagram for hundreds of millions of daily users: people upload photos and videos, follow accounts, read a personalized feed, publish expiring stories, and receive media and interaction updates reliably.
successSignals: Separate durable media metadata and social graph state from object storage, CDN delivery, and rebuildable feed projections.
Choose fanout-on-write, fanout-on-read, or a hybrid strategy for normal and celebrity accounts.
Design resumable uploads, asynchronous processing, privacy and moderation checks, and idempotent interaction events.
Bound feed reads and story expiry work while making freshness, deletion, and regional failure behavior explicit.

functional: Upload photos and videos, generate multiple renditions, and publish a post or 24-hour story.
Follow and unfollow users, read a personalized feed, and view a profile timeline.
Like, comment, share, and receive notifications for eligible interactions.
Search users and hashtags while enforcing private accounts, blocks, moderation, deletion, and data export rules.
nonFunctional: A post's metadata and ownership must be durable before publication; media processing may complete asynchronously.
Target p95 under 200 ms for a cached feed page and under 2 seconds for normal media availability after upload.
Serve popular media through a CDN, isolate celebrity fanout, and avoid blocking reads on recommendation or moderation workers.
Tolerate resumable upload retries, worker failures, duplicate events, story expiry races, and regional degradation.
scaleAssumptions: 500 million daily active users, 100 million media uploads per day, and 10 million concurrent feed or story viewers at peak.
Most users follow fewer than 1,000 accounts; a small number of creators have tens of millions of followers.
Each upload produces several image or video renditions; originals and derivatives are stored in object storage with lifecycle tiers.
Stories expire after 24 hours, but deletion and privacy changes must invalidate them immediately from serving paths.

metrics.label: Media upload rate
metrics.description: 100M uploads per day; provision ingestion, object storage, and processing for event bursts.

metrics.label: Feed read latency
metrics.description: Serve a bounded cursor page from projections and cache without scanning the social graph.

metrics.label: Media readiness
metrics.description: Upload acknowledgement is immediate; normal renditions become playable asynchronously within this target.

metrics.label: Story lifetime
metrics.description: TTL is a serving rule, backed by durable state and explicit deletion or moderation invalidation.

dataFlow.title: Upload and publish media
dataFlow.description: The client uploads to object storage; metadata, ownership, visibility, checksum, and moderation state are committed before publication.

dataFlow.title: Maintain the social graph
dataFlow.description: Follow/unfollow edges are conditionally written and publish graph events that affect feed candidates and authorization.

dataFlow.title: Build home-feed candidates
dataFlow.description: Fanout workers push ordinary posts to follower partitions, while high-follower accounts are pulled or hybrid-fanned out at read time.

dataFlow.title: Serve feed and stories
dataFlow.description: Feed and story services merge ranked candidates, check visibility and expiry, and return cursor/freshness metadata.

dataFlow.title: Process interactions and moderation
dataFlow.description: Like/comment/report events update projections, notifications, discovery, and safety queues asynchronously with repairable state.

architecture.title: Instagram reference architecture
architecture.summary: Clients upload directly to object storage, while durable content and graph services publish events to media workers, hybrid feed fanout, CDN manifests, and interaction consumers.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Clients upload media, browse feeds and stories, and submit interactions.

layers.label: Source and graph layer
layers.description: Durable content, media metadata, ownership, visibility, and social relationships.

layers.label: Media and feed plane
layers.description: Asynchronous processing, object delivery, and hybrid feed projections.

layers.label: Extensions and operations
layers.description: Notifications, moderation, ranking, analytics, expiry, and observability consume events independently.

keyPaths.label: Upload and publish path
keyPaths.description: Client -> signed object upload -> content service -> durable metadata -> media workers.

keyPaths.label: Feed read path
keyPaths.description: Client -> feed service -> projection/cache, with hot-author merge and CDN media URLs.

keyPaths.label: Hybrid publication path
keyPaths.description: Content event -> fanout strategy -> follower projections or pull-on-read.

deepDives.title: Fanout strategy and hot creators
points: For Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform, a user's feed must contain only visible, non-expired content from the current graph and policy versions.
Design for the failure case where celebrity fanout, upload bursts, deletes, and policy changes must not overwhelm writes or expose content; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Media processing and lifecycle
points: For Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform, a user's feed must contain only visible, non-expired content from the current graph and policy versions.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Graph authorization and moderation
points: For Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform, a user's feed must contain only visible, non-expired content from the current graph and policy versions.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

tradeoffs.title: Fanout-on-write versus fanout-on-read
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use a hybrid: push normal creators to feed partitions and pull high-fanout creators when the viewer reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Pure push creates massive write amplification; pure pull makes home-feed latency and ranking expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Strong graph reads versus cached feed
tradeoffs.recommendation: Commit graph edges strongly and let feed projections converge with invalidation and policy checks on read.
tradeoffs.caution: A feed cache without visibility checks can show content after unfollow, block, or delete.

tradeoffs.title: Original media retention versus delivery cost
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep originals in durable tiered storage and generate policy-approved renditions behind a CDN.
tradeoffs.caution: Keeping every rendition hot is expensive; deleting originals too early prevents reprocessing.

commonMistakes: Fanning out every celebrity post to every follower synchronously.
Putting media transcoding on the publish request path.
Ignoring block/private-account/delete checks during feed reads.
Using notification delivery as proof that an interaction committed.
Having no replay path for feed or graph projection drift.

followUps.question: How do you handle a creator with 100M followers?
followUps.answer: Use hybrid fanout, pull-time ranking, cached creator posts, and isolate the creator's partitions from ordinary writes.

followUps.question: What if a private account changes visibility?
followUps.answer: Commit the policy version, invalidate affected feed items, enforce the policy at read time, and audit deletion from projections.

followUps.question: How do you process a video upload spike?
followUps.answer: Use direct object uploads, prioritized durable queues, elastic transcode pools, and a status endpoint that never waits for renditions.

rubric.description: The answer defines media durability, graph consistency, hybrid feed fanout, ranking, visibility, moderation, and async interaction handling, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the Instagram's media, graph, feed, and story platform consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
